risk: Deeply nested brace patterns can exhaust the stack and terminate lint/CI processing.
reason: GitHub advisory reports no patched version; official npm latest is 3.0.3 and micromatch 4.0.8 still depends on braces ^3.0.3. No unpublished version or unsupported fork is installed.
scope: Exact audited ESLint dev-tool dependency path only. Application code has no direct calls and 73 local production NFT traces contain no braces/micromatch/fast-glob entries; this is candidate-build evidence, not a universal runtime guarantee.
mitigation: Keep ESLint glob settings static and repository-controlled; review PR configuration changes before trusted execution. Preserve exact-version/path audit matching, reject other High/Critical findings and recheck deployed traces before release. CI denial-of-service risk remains.
upstreamPlan: Recheck upstream before expiry and upgrade immediately when a supported patched release or dependency path is available. Expiry blocks the gate automatically.

risk: A recursive object graph can exhaust the stack during configuration merging.
reason: Prisma 7.10.0 pins @prisma/config to deepmerge-ts 7.1.5; the patched deepmerge-ts 8.x is outside Prisma's declared dependency and cannot be forced without unsupported compatibility risk.
scope: Prisma CLI and trusted build/migration configuration only; public requests do not supply objects to Prisma configuration merging.
mitigation: Pin dependencies, keep Prisma configuration static and repository-controlled, reject all other high/critical advisories, and track Prisma for a compatible fixed release.
upstreamPlan: Upgrade immediately when a stable Prisma release adopts deepmerge-ts 8.x or another patched implementation.
